To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the shapes of colour-producing nanostructures in avain feather barbs are determined by phase-separation of β-keratins from the cytoplplasm of medullary cell and by capillary flow through the drying of medulllary cells.

the characteristic shapes and sizes of colour-producing, intracellulr, spongy β-keratin medullary nanostructures of avian feathers are produced by phase separation during the polymerization of medullary keratin protein, and that the hollow morphology of the medullary cell is likely to be a consequence of capillary flow during drying.

the shapes of colour-producing, channel-type nanostructures in the barb medullary cells develop during phase separation and are similar to those produced by spinodal decomposition, while the shapes of colourless, spherical-type nanostructures in barb medullaries are similar to those of nucleation and growth.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the origin of the structural colours in avian feathers, and we propose a mechanism for the formation of the nanostructures responsible for these colours.
the development of colour-producing nanostructures in the avian integument and the role of phase separation in the development of these nanostructures.
the origin and evolution of the colour-producing nanostructures in aves and their possible role in the development of avian colour vision.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

β-keratin proteins in medullary cells self-assemble into nanostructures of different morphologies by phase separation of an intracellular, unstable mixture of protein and water, a process known as spinodal decomposition.

the development of the colour-producing nanostructure of medullary keratin in feather barbs proceeds by intracellular self-assembling processes that are driven by phase separation of the β-keratin proteins from the cytoplams of medullary barb cells.
the colour-producing nanostructures of avian barbs are formed by a combination of phase separation and capillary flow during feather development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the shapes and sizes of colour-producing nanostructures are determined mainly by the physical properties of the β-keratin polymer, and the physical and chemical properties of the cytoplasm, and not by the genetic code of β-keratins or the cell membrane.

the colour-producing, intracelluar nanostructures of medulla β-keratin are formed by self-assembly of the β-keratin proteins during the phase separation process of the protein solution in the medullar cells.

the colour-producing, intracelluar, medullary β -keratin nanostructures of avian feather rami are produced during the phase separation and polymerization of β -keratin protein, a process that occurs within the cytoplasm and the endoplasmic space.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the shapes of colour-producing nanostructures in avain barb rami are produced by intracellular self-assemblies of β-keratins during phase separation, and are not determined by biological prepatterns created by cell membranes, intermediate filaments or endoplasmic networks.
the shapes of colour-producing β keratin nanostructures in the medullaries of avian feather rami are determined by self-assembly and phase separation of β keratin protein.
the development of the nanostructure in the medullar cells of avian feather rami is a process of phase separation of β keratin proteins from the cytoplamic fluid.
